questions.q: Why do governance programs need a council or committee structure in addition to individual roles like owners and stewards?
options: Owners and stewards are not allowed to make any decisions on their own
Data disputes often cross domain boundaries, and no single owner's authority covers more than one domain
Committees replace the need for any individual accountability
It is purely a legal formality with no practical function
questions.explain: A standing, cross-functional body exists specifically to resolve issues that fall between or across individual domains and owners.

questions.q: In the typical layered structure described in this lesson, what does the governance council primarily do?
options: Replaces the need for an executive sponsor
Writes the detailed technical validation rules for one specific domain
Sets overall strategy, sponsors the program, and makes the highest-level trade-off decisions
Handles day-to-day customer support tickets
questions.explain: The council sits at the top, focused on strategy and top-level trade-offs; the committee below it handles operational policy and disputes.

questions.q: What is a 'working group' in this structure typically responsible for?
options: Detailed, domain- or initiative-specific standards work, escalating to the main committee only when stuck
Approving the entire company's annual budget
Negotiating contracts with regulators directly
Hiring and firing data owners
questions.explain: Working groups do the detailed subject-matter work; they escalate upward only when an issue can't be resolved at their level.

questions.q: Which of these is a core responsibility of a governance committee, per this lesson?
options: Replacing stewards entirely so no stewardship role is needed
Setting the company's stock price
Writing every employee's individual performance review
Resolving cross-domain disputes that no single data owner can settle alone
questions.explain: The committee approves policy, resolves cross-domain disputes, formally empowers owners/stewards, and prioritizes issues.

questions.q: How should a smaller organization right-size this structure, according to this lesson?
options: It should assign every employee to the committee
It should skip governance structure entirely until it has over 10,000 employees
It can compress council and committee into a single cross-functional group under an executive sponsor, as long as some standing forum exists
It must implement all three layers exactly as described, with no exceptions
questions.explain: What matters is that a standing, cross-functional forum exists above individual data owners — not the exact number of layers.
